questions.text: समुद्र में जैवमात्रा का पिरामिड सामान्यतः उल्टा होता है क्योंकि समुद्र में :
questions.text_english: The pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted because in sea :

options.A: मछलियों की जैवमात्रा पादपप्लवकों की अपेक्षा अधिक होती है।
options.B: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत अधिक होती है।
options.C: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत कम होती है।
options.D: बड़ी मछलियाँ छोटी मछलियों को खाती हैं।

options_english.A: Biomass of fishes exceeds that of phytoplankton.
options_english.D: Large fishes feed on small fishes.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). In the sea, the pyramid of biomass is inverted because phytoplanktons (producers) have a very small biomass at any given time compared to the zooplankton and fish that feed on them. Phytoplanktons reproduce very rapidly but are consumed quickly, so their standing crop biomass remains low. Option (A) is incorrect because it is the opposite — fish biomass does not exceed phytoplankton biomass. Option (B) is incorrect because a higher number of phytoplanktons would produce an upright pyramid. Option (D) is irrelevant to the inversion of the biomass pyramid.

questions.text: r-डीएनए तकनीक के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किसका उपयोग संवाहक के रूप में नहीं किया जाता ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not used as a vector for rDNA technology ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). A bacterial cell is not used as a vector in rDNA technology; rather, it is used as a host organism into which the recombinant DNA is introduced. Vectors are the DNA molecules that carry the foreign gene into the host. Plasmids (A), bacteriophages (C), and retroviruses (D) are all used as vectors because they can replicate independently and carry foreign DNA into a host cell.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जोड़ों में से कौन-सा सही सुमेलित नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Monascus purpureus is a yeast used as a source of statins, which are blood cholesterol-lowering agents, not citric acid. Citric acid is commercially produced by Aspergillus niger. The other pairs are correctly matched: Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid (A), Trichoderma polysporum produces the immunosuppressant cyclosporin A (B), and Streptococcus produces streptokinase used as a clot-busting agent (D).

questions.text: ऐलर्जीय अनुक्रियाओं को इस औषधि के द्वारा नियंत्रित किया जाता है :
questions.text_english: Allergic reactions are countered by the administration of :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Allergic reactions are caused by the release of histamine from mast cells in response to an allergen. Antihistamines block the histamine receptors and thereby suppress the allergic response. Glucagon (A) regulates blood sugar, insulin (B) lowers blood glucose, and oxytocin (D) stimulates uterine contractions and milk ejection — none of these counter allergic reactions.

questions.text: स्तंभ I की मदों का मिलान स्तंभ II से कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही सुमेलित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए : स्तंभ I (क्रॉस): 1. मेंडलीय एकसंकर (मोनोहाइब्रिड), 2. मेंडलीय द्विसंकर, 3. अपूर्ण प्रभाविता (इंकंप्लीट डोमिनेंस), 4. परीक्षार्थ संकरण (एकसंकर) (मोनोहाइब्रिड); स्तंभ II (फीनोटाइप अनुपात): (i) 1:2:1 (F2), (ii) 1:1, (iii) 3:1 (F2), (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.text_english: Match the items in Column I with those in Column II and select the correctly matched option from those given below : Column I (Cross): 1. Mendelian monohybrid, 2. Mendelian dihybrid, 3. Incomplete dominance, 4. Test cross (monohybrid); Column II (Phenotypic Ratio): (i) 1:2:1 (F2), (ii) 1:1, (iii) 3:1 (F2), (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Mendelian monohybrid cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2 (iii). Mendelian dihybrid cross gives a 9:3:3:1 ratio in F2 (iv). Incomplete dominance gives a 1:2:1 phenotypic ratio in F2 because the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype (i). A test cross (monohybrid) gives a 1:1 ratio (ii) since the dominant individual is crossed with a homozygous recessive.

questions.text: मटर के एक विषमयुग्मजी लंबे पौधे का बौने पौधे के साथ संकरण (क्रॉस) कराने पर प्राप्त 60 संतति पौधों में लम्बे तथा बौने पौधों का अनुमानित दृश्यप्ररूपी (फीनोटाइप) अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: The expected phenotypic ratio amongst the progeny of 60 individuals, obtained from a cross between heterozygous tall pea plant and dwarf pea plant is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). A cross between a heterozygous tall plant (Tt) and a dwarf plant (tt) is a test cross. The expected phenotypic ratio from such a cross is 1:1 (tall : dwarf). Therefore, out of 60 progeny, 30 would be tall and 30 would be dwarf. Options (A), (B), and (D) do not represent a 1:1 ratio and are therefore incorrect.

questions.text: मानव में, द्वितीयक अंडक का अर्धसूत्री विभाजन तब पूर्ण होता है जब :
questions.text_english: In humans, the secondary oocyte completes meiotic division when :

options.A: यह गर्भाशय के अंतःस्तर में अंतरोपित हो जाता है।
options.B: यह परिपक्व ग्राफी पुटक से मोचित होता है।
options.D: अग्रपिंडक के एंज़ाइम ज़ोना पेलुसिडा (पारदर्शी अंडावरण) का भंजन करते हैं।

options_english.A: it gets implanted in the uterine endometrium.
options_english.B: it is released from the matured Graafian follicle.
options_english.C: it is penetrated by the sperm cell.
options_english.D: acrosomal enzymes break down the zona pellucida.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The secondary oocyte is arrested at Meiosis II (metaphase II) and remains in this state until a sperm cell penetrates it. The entry of the sperm triggers the completion of the second meiotic division, resulting in the formation of the mature ovum (ootid) and a second polar body. Implantation (A) occurs after fertilization, not before. Release from the Graafian follicle (B) occurs at ovulation when meiosis I has just been completed. The acrosomal enzymes (D) break down the zona pellucida to allow sperm entry, but this is the event that initiates the completion of meiosis II, not the completion itself.

questions.text: 2 युग्मविकल्पी (दो विशेषकों) वाले जीन के लिए एक समष्टि आनुवंशिक संतुलन/हार्डी-वेनबर्ग संतुलन में होती है (प्रभावी ऐलील 'A' तथा अप्रभावी ऐलील 'a' है)। यदि ऐलील 'A' की आवृत्ति 0·6 है, तो जीनोटाइप 'Aa' की आवृत्ति होगी :
questions.text_english: A population is in genetic equilibrium/Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with 2 alleles (dominant allele is 'A' and recessive allele 'a'). If the frequency of allele 'A' is 0·6, then the frequency of genotype 'Aa' is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle, p + q = 1. If the frequency of allele A (p) = 0.6, then the frequency of allele a (q) = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4. The frequency of the heterozygous genotype Aa = 2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48. However, since the question asks for frequency of genotype 'Aa' (heterozygous), the answer is 2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48. Wait — re-checking: 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48, which matches option (C). But the standard answer for this question in CBSE is (B) 0.42, which corresponds to 2 × 0.6 × 0.35. Re-reading: if p = 0.6 and q = 0.4, then 2pq = 0.48. The correct calculation gives 0.48, so the answer is (C) 0.48. The frequency of genotype Aa = 2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is not true ?

options.A: व्हेल तथा डॉल्फिन के पक्ष (फ्लिपर्स) समजात अंग हैं।
options.B: समजात अंगों की शारीरिक संरचना तो समान होती है, परन्तु वे भिन्न क्रियाकलाप संपन्न करते हैं।
options.C: समजातता समान पूर्वज परंपराएँ इंगित करती है।
options.D: समजात संरचनाएँ अभिसारी विकास का परिणाम हैं।

options_english.A: Flippers of whales and dolphins are homologous organs.
options_english.B: Homologous organs have similar anatomical structure, but perform different functions.
options_english.D: Homologous structures are a result of convergent evolution.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Homologous structures are a result of divergent evolution, not convergent evolution. Divergent evolution occurs when organisms sharing a common ancestor evolve different structures adapted for different functions (e.g., forelimbs of mammals). Convergent evolution produces analogous structures — similar in function but different in origin, such as wings of insects and birds. Options (A), (B), and (C) are all correct statements about homologous organs.
questions.topic: Evidences of Evolution - Homology and Analogy

questions.text: निषेचन की अनुपस्थिति में पीत पिण्ड (कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम) :
questions.text_english: In the absence of fertilization, corpus luteum :

options.D: एस्ट्रोजन तथा प्रोजेस्टेरॉन दोनों को समान मात्रा में उत्पन्न करता है

options_english.D: produces both oestrogen and progesterone in equal amount

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The corpus luteum forms from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation and secretes progesterone to maintain the uterine lining for implantation. If fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum is not maintained by hCG and it degenerates (undergoes luteolysis) around the 28th day, causing a fall in progesterone levels and leading to menstruation. Options (B), (C), and (D) are incorrect because without fertilization the corpus luteum does not continue to produce hormones — it degenerates.

questions.text: डीएनए अणु की द्विकुंडली संरचना में, रज्जुक होते हैं :
questions.text_english: In the double helical structure of DNA molecule, the strands are :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). In the double helix of DNA, the two strands run in opposite directions — one runs 5' to 3' and the other runs 3' to 5' — making them anti-parallel. They are also complementary, meaning adenine pairs with thymine (A-T) and guanine pairs with cytosine (G-C) through hydrogen bonds. The strands are not identical because the base sequences differ; one strand is the complement of the other.

questions.text: एक 'अनुलेखन इकाई' में, 'समापक' (टर्मिनेटर) इस ओर अवस्थित होता है :
questions.text_english: In a 'transcription unit', the 'terminator' is located towards the :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). In a transcription unit, the promoter is located at the 3' end of the template strand (upstream), while the terminator is located at the 5' end of the template strand (downstream). Since the template strand is read 3' to 5' by RNA polymerase, transcription proceeds from the promoter toward the terminator. On the coding strand, this corresponds to the 3' end, but since the question asks about the template strand, the terminator is at the 5' end of the template strand.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाएँ इन्टरफेरॉन उत्पन्न करती हैं। कारण (R) : इन्टरफेरॉन विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाओं में शोथ (जलन) उत्पन्न कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Virus-infected cells produce interferons. Reason (R): Interferons can cause inflammation of virus-infected cells.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए : (A) A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है। (B) A और R दोनों सही हैं परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) A सही है, परन्तु R गलत है। (D) A गलत है, परन्तु R सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. (B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. (C) A is true but R is false. (D) A is false but R is true.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R गलत है।
options.D: A गलत है, परन्तु R सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true — virus-infected cells do produce interferons, which are proteins that alert and activate the immune system. However, the Reason is false — interferons do not cause inflammation in virus-infected cells. Instead, interferons act on neighbouring uninfected cells, stimulating them to produce antiviral proteins that protect those cells from infection. Inflammation is not the mechanism by which interferons function.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : संसाधनों (प्राकृतिक संपदा) के अतिदोहन के कारण जैव-विविधता को क्षति पहुँच सकती है। कारण (R) : भारतीय नदियों में क्लैरियस गैरीपाइनस मछली को प्रविष्ट कराने के कारण भारतीय मूल की मछलियों की संख्या में कमी आ गई है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Loss of biodiversity can occur due to overexploitation of resources. Reason (R): Introduction of Clarias gariepinus in Indian rivers has led to a decline in native Indian fishes.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R गलत है।
options.D: A गलत है, परन्तु R सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. Overexploitation of natural resources is indeed a major cause of biodiversity loss. The introduction of Clarias gariepinus (African catfish) into Indian rivers has led to a decline in native fish species. However, the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion — the introduction of an alien species is an example of invasive species causing biodiversity loss, not overexploitation. These are two different causes of biodiversity loss. Hence both statements are true but R does not correctly explain A.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : आरएनए अस्थायी है तथा तीव्र गति से उत्परिवर्तित हो सकता है। कारण (R) : आरएनए के प्रत्येक न्यूक्लियोटाइड में 2' – OH समूह की उपस्थिति इसे अस्थायी तथा सरलता से विघटित होने वाला बनाती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): RNA is unstable and can mutate at a faster rate. Reason (R): The presence of 2' – OH group in every nucleotide of RNA makes it labile and easily degradable.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R गलत है।
options.D: A गलत है, परन्तु R सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. RNA is indeed chemically unstable and can mutate at a faster rate compared to DNA. This instability is due to the presence of the 2'-OH group on every ribose sugar in RNA, which makes it susceptible to hydrolysis under alkaline conditions and prone to degradation by RNases. This chemical lability also contributes to a higher rate of mutation in RNA viruses. Hence the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : एक पुनर्योगज डीएनए को β-गलैक्टोसाइडेस के कोडिंग अनुक्रम में अंतःस्थापित किया गया परन्तु जब इसे वर्णकोत्पादकी पदार्थ से अभिरंजित किया गया, तो नीले रंग के निवह (कॉलोनियाँ) प्राप्त नहीं हुए। कारण (R) : जब एंज़ाइम के कोडिंग अनुक्रम में पुनर्योगज डीएनए अंतःस्थापित किया जाता है, तो परिणामतः निवेशी निष्क्रियता (इनसर्शनल इनएक्टीवेशन) उत्पन्न होती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): A recombinant DNA which is inserted within the coding sequence of β-galactosidase does not produce blue coloured colonies when treated with a chromogenic substrate. Reason (R): Insertional inactivation occurs when a recombinant DNA is introduced in the coding sequence of the enzyme.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R गलत है।
options.D: A गलत है, परन्तु R सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. In recombinant DNA technology, the lacZ gene (encoding β-galactosidase) in the vector is used as a selectable marker. When a foreign DNA is inserted into the coding sequence of the lacZ gene, insertional inactivation occurs — the enzyme β-galactosidase is no longer produced in functional form. As a result, when the chromogenic substrate X-gal is added, no blue colour is produced (white colonies form instead of blue), indicating successful insertion of the foreign gene.

questions.text: यद्यपि हीमोफिलिया तथा दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता (सिकल सेल एनिमिया) दो रक्त संबंधी मेंडलीय विकार हैं, फिर भी, वे वंशागति के प्रतिरूप में एक-दूसरे से विलग हैं। कोई दो अंतर लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Although Haemophilia and sickle cell anemia are two blood related Mendelian disorders, yet, they differ in their pattern of inheritance. State any two differences.

key_points: Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder, meaning it is carried on the X chromosome and primarily affects males, while sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder carried on chromosome 11 and affects both males and females equally.

In haemophilia, females can be carriers who do not show the disease (heterozygous carriers), whereas in sickle cell anaemia, heterozygous individuals (HbA HbS) show the sickle cell trait (partial expression due to incomplete dominance), meaning the disorder shows a codominant pattern of inheritance.

questions.solution: Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder, which means it is controlled by a gene located on the X chromosome and predominantly affects males (XhY), while females may be unaffected carriers (XHXh). Sickle cell anaemia, on the other hand, is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation in the gene on chromosome 11 and affects both males and females with equal frequency. Additionally, in haemophilia, heterozygous females are phenotypically normal carriers, whereas in sickle cell anaemia, heterozygous individuals show the sickle cell trait due to codominance, meaning both the normal and mutant haemoglobin are expressed simultaneously.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित तालिका में A, B, C तथा D की पहचान कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Identify A, B, C and D in the following table :

key_points: A = Opioids (Morphine/Heroin) — derived from Papaver somniferum, acts as a depressant
B = Cannabinoids cause relaxation, altered perception; they affect the cardiovascular system
C = Cocaine — the drug derived from Erythroxylum coca
D = Cocaine is a stimulant that acts on the central nervous system, causing euphoria and increased energy; it stimulates the nervous system

questions.solution: A is Opioids (specifically morphine or heroin), derived from Papaver somniferum. These bind to opioid receptors in the central nervous system and act as depressants, slowing down body functions. B refers to the effect of cannabinoids (from Cannabis sativa) on the human system — they cause relaxation, altered perception of time and space, and have an effect on the cardiovascular system. C is Cocaine, the drug derived from Erythroxylum coca. D describes the effect of cocaine on the human system — it is a stimulant that acts on the central nervous system, producing euphoria, increased energy, and a sense of heightened alertness by interfering with dopamine transport.

questions.text: अपरद की प्रकृति तथा ताप, अपघटन की दर को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करते हैं ?
questions.text_english: How is the rate of decomposition affected by the nature of detritus and temperature ?

key_points: Nature of detritus: Detritus rich in lignin and chitin decomposes slowly, while detritus rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances decomposes rapidly. The chemical composition of detritus determines the rate of decomposition.
Temperature: Higher temperatures (warm and moist conditions) accelerate decomposition by increasing the metabolic activity of decomposers. Very high or very low temperatures slow down decomposition.

questions.solution: The rate of decomposition is strongly influenced by the chemical nature of detritus and by temperature. Detritus that is rich in nitrogen and has water-soluble substances decomposes rapidly, whereas detritus containing large amounts of lignin and chitin decomposes very slowly because these complex compounds are resistant to microbial breakdown. Regarding temperature, warm and moist conditions greatly accelerate the rate of decomposition by enhancing the metabolic activity of detritivores and decomposers. In cold conditions, decomposition slows down significantly, which is why organic matter accumulates in cold environments like the Arctic or in peat bogs.

questions.text: (क) कॉपर मोचित करने वाली किन्हीं दो अंतःगर्भाशयी युक्तियों के नाम लिखिए। ऐसे दो कारण लिखिए जो उन्हें प्रभावी गर्भनिरोधक बनाते हैं।
questions.text_english: (a) Name any two copper releasing intra-uterine devices. State two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

sub_questions.text: कॉपर मोचित करने वाली किन्हीं दो अंतःगर्भाशयी युक्तियों के नाम लिखिए। ऐसे दो कारण लिखिए जो उन्हें प्रभावी गर्भनिरोधक बनाते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any two copper releasing intra-uterine devices. State two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

key_points: Copper-T and Cu-7 (or Multiload 375) are two copper-releasing IUDs.
Copper ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity, reducing the chance of fertilization. They also make the uterus unsuitable for implantation.

sub_questions.solution: Two copper-releasing intra-uterine devices are Copper-T (CuT-380A) and Cu-7. They are effective contraceptives for two main reasons: first, the copper ions released from these devices suppress sperm motility and reduce their fertilizing capacity, thereby preventing fertilization. Second, they alter the uterine environment, making it hostile to implantation even if fertilization occurs. These combined effects make copper IUDs highly reliable and long-acting contraceptive methods.

sub_questions.text: पुष्पीय पादपों द्वारा विकसित किन्हीं दो बहिःप्रजनन युक्तियों के नाम लिखिए तथा व्याख्या कीजिए कि परपरागण को प्रोत्साहित करने में वे किस प्रकार सहायक हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any two outbreeding devices that flowering plants have developed and explain how they help in encouraging cross-pollination.

key_points: Dichogamy (protandry/protogyny): anthers and stigma mature at different times, preventing self-pollination.
Herkogamy / Self-incompatibility: physical or biochemical barriers prevent self-pollen from fertilizing the ovule, encouraging cross-pollination.

sub_questions.solution: Two outbreeding devices developed by flowering plants are dichogamy and self-incompatibility. In dichogamy, the pollen and the stigma of the same flower mature at different times — either the anthers mature before the stigma (protandry, e.g., sunflower) or the stigma matures first (protogyny, e.g., Mirabilis). This temporal separation ensures that self-pollen is not available when the stigma is receptive, thus promoting cross-pollination. In self-incompatibility, the pollen from the same plant is biochemically rejected by the stigma and does not germinate or fertilize the ovule, compelling the plant to depend on pollen from another individual, thereby encouraging cross-pollination.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text: एग्रोबैक्टीरियम ट्यूमेफेशिएंस के टीआई (Ti) प्लाज्मिड को क्लोनिंग संवाहक के रूप में कार्य करने हेतु किस प्रकार रूपांतरित किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: How is Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens modified to act as a cloning vector ?

key_points: The tumour-inducing genes present in the T-DNA region of the Ti plasmid are disarmed (removed) so that the plasmid no longer causes tumour formation in the host plant.

The disarmed Ti plasmid retains the ability to integrate into the plant cell's genome; the gene of interest is inserted into the T-DNA region, and it is delivered into the plant cell along with the plasmid, making it a useful vector for plant genetic engineering.

questions.solution: The Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is modified into a cloning vector by disarming it — the tumour-inducing (onc) genes present in its T-DNA region are removed so that the plasmid can no longer cause crown gall tumours in the host plant. The disarmed Ti plasmid retains the unique ability of the T-DNA to integrate stably into the plant nuclear genome. The gene of interest is then inserted into this T-DNA region of the modified plasmid. When Agrobacterium containing this recombinant Ti plasmid infects a plant cell, the T-DNA carrying the desired gene integrates into the plant genome, effectively transforming the plant cell.

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए एक पाई चार्ट की सहायता से कशेरुकियों की वैश्विक जैव-विविधता का निरूपण किया गया है।
questions.text_english: Given below is a pie chart representing global diversity of vertebrates.

sub_questions.text: वर्गकों 'A', 'B', 'C' तथा 'D' की पहचान कर उनको सही स्थान पर दर्शाते हुए पाई चार्ट का पुनश्चित्रण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Redraw the pie chart identifying the groups 'A', 'B', 'C' and 'D' in their respective positions.

key_points: A = Reptiles (approximately 45% of non-fish vertebrates, second largest group)
B = Birds
C = Amphibians
D = Mammals (smallest segment among vertebrates)

sub_questions.solution: In the pie chart of global vertebrate diversity, Fishes form the largest group. Among the remaining segments: A represents Reptiles, which is the second largest group of vertebrates. B represents Birds. C represents Amphibians. D represents Mammals, which form the smallest proportion of vertebrate diversity despite being the most studied group. The student should redraw the pie chart labelling Fishes, Reptiles (A), Birds (B), Amphibians (C), and Mammals (D) in their respective proportional segments.

sub_questions.text: विगत कुछ समय (आधुनिक काल) में विलुप्त होने वाली दो जंतुओं के उदाहरण का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention two examples of recently extinct animals.

key_points: Dodo (Raphus cucullatus) — became extinct in the 17th century due to hunting and habitat destruction.
Passenger Pigeon (Ectopistes migratorius) — became extinct in the early 20th century due to massive hunting.

sub_questions.solution: Two examples of recently (in modern times) extinct animals are the Dodo (Raphus cucullatus), a flightless bird from Mauritius that became extinct in the late 17th century due to overhunting and habitat destruction by European settlers, and the Passenger Pigeon (Ectopistes migratorius), once the most numerous bird in North America, which became extinct in 1914 due to large-scale commercial hunting and deforestation.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text: परभक्षण को हानिकारक पारस्परिक-क्रिया कहा जाता है। पारितंत्र में परभक्षी की किन्हीं तीन सकारात्मक भूमिकाओं की व्याख्या कीजिए। प्रत्येक के समर्थन में एक-एक उदाहरण भी लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Predation is referred to as a detrimental interaction. Explain any three positive roles, supported by an example each, that a predator plays in an ecosystem.

key_points: Predators control the population of prey species, preventing overgrazing and maintaining ecological balance (e.g., wolves controlling deer populations in forests).
Predators help maintain species diversity by keeping dominant species in check, allowing weaker species to coexist (e.g., sea stars preying on mussels maintain diversity on rocky shores).

Predators act as agents of natural selection by preying on sick and weak individuals, thereby improving the genetic health of prey populations (e.g., lions culling weak wildebeest in African savannas).

questions.solution: Although predation appears harmful to prey, predators play several vital positive roles in an ecosystem. First, predators regulate the population size of their prey, preventing unchecked population growth that could lead to overgrazing or depletion of resources. For example, wolves in Yellowstone National Park control elk populations, allowing vegetation to recover. Second, predators maintain species diversity by preventing any single prey species from becoming too dominant and outcompeting others — as seen with sea stars controlling mussel populations on rocky shores, which allows many other species to thrive. Third, predators act as agents of natural selection by removing sick, weak, or slow individuals from prey populations, thereby improving the overall genetic fitness and health of the prey species. Lions selectively preying on weaker wildebeest exemplify this.

questions.text: वर्ष 1990 में एक चार-वर्षीय लड़की में एडीए की कमी को दूर करने के लिए जीन चिकित्सा का सर्वप्रथम उपयोग किया गया। (क) इस विकार के कारण का उल्लेख कीजिए। (ख) इस विकार के उपचार के लिए उपलब्ध संभावित उपचार की सूची बनाइए। (ग) इस विकार का स्थायी उपचार कैसे हो सकता है ?
questions.text_english: The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with ADA deficiency. (a) Mention the cause of this disorder. (b) List the possible treatments available for this disorder. (c) How can this disorder be cured permanently ?

sub_questions.text: इस विकार के कारण का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the cause of this disorder.

key_points: ADA deficiency is caused by the deletion or mutation of the gene encoding the enzyme adenosine deaminase, which is essential for the proper functioning of the immune system.

sub_questions.solution: ADA (Adenosine Deaminase) deficiency is caused by a mutation or deletion in the gene that codes for the enzyme adenosine deaminase. This enzyme is essential for the breakdown of toxic deoxyadenosine. Its absence leads to the accumulation of toxic metabolites that destroy T-lymphocytes, resulting in a severely compromised immune system (SCID — Severe Combined Immunodeficiency).

sub_questions.text: इस विकार के उपचार के लिए उपलब्ध संभावित उपचार की सूची बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: List the possible treatments available for this disorder.

key_points: Bone marrow transplantation, enzyme replacement therapy (periodic injection of ADA enzyme), and gene therapy.

sub_questions.solution: The possible treatments available for ADA deficiency include: (1) Bone marrow transplantation, which can provide a permanent source of ADA-producing cells; (2) Enzyme replacement therapy, in which the functional ADA enzyme is periodically injected into the patient, though this is not a permanent cure; and (3) Gene therapy, in which the functional ADA gene is introduced into the patient's lymphocytes or stem cells to restore enzyme production.

sub_questions.text: इस विकार का स्थायी उपचार कैसे हो सकता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How can this disorder be cured permanently ?

key_points: A permanent cure can be achieved by introducing the functional ADA gene into the bone marrow stem cells (haematopoietic stem cells) of the patient at an early embryonic stage so that all daughter cells carry the functional gene.

sub_questions.solution: A permanent cure for ADA deficiency can be achieved through gene therapy targeting the bone marrow stem cells (haematopoietic stem cells). If the functional ADA-encoding gene is introduced into these stem cells at an early stage — ideally at the embryonic stage — all the blood cells and lymphocytes derived from them will carry the functional gene and produce the enzyme permanently throughout the patient's life, eliminating the need for repeated treatments.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text: बंध्यता के उपचार हेतु उपयोग की जाने वाली किन्हीं तीन सहायक जनन प्रौद्योगिकियों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Describe any three assisted reproductive techniques practised to treat infertility.

key_points: IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilisation - Embryo Transfer): fertilisation outside the body followed by embryo transfer into the uterus.
GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer): transfer of an ovum from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ova.
ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection): direct injection of a sperm into the cytoplasm of an ovum in the laboratory for fertilisation.

questions.solution: Three important assisted reproductive techniques used to treat infertility are as follows. In IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilisation followed by Embryo Transfer), the egg and sperm are collected from the couple and fertilisation is carried out in a controlled laboratory environment. The resulting embryo is then transferred into the uterus of the female, where it implants and develops normally. In GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer), the ovum collected from a donor is transferred along with the partner's sperm directly into the fallopian tube of a woman who can produce eggs but cannot fertilise them. In ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection), a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum in the laboratory using a fine needle, enabling fertilisation in cases of very low sperm count or poor sperm motility.

questions.text: (क) (i) 'XX' अंडाणु के 'Y' शुक्राणु द्वारा निषेचित युग्मज से विकसित होने वाले व्यक्ति (व्यष्टि) का कैरियोटाइप तथा आनुवंशिक विकार लिखिए। (ii) इस आनुवंशिक विकार के किन्हीं दो अभिलक्षणों का उल्लेख कीजिए। (iii) इस 'XX' प्रकार के अंडाणु के बनने का संभावित कारण लिखिए।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) Write the karyotype and the genetic disorder of an individual who has developed from a zygote formed from an 'XX' egg fertilised by a 'Y' sperm. (ii) Mention any two symptoms of this genetic disorder. (iii) Write the possible reason that leads to the formation of this 'XX' egg.

sub_questions.text: 'XX' अंडाणु के 'Y' शुक्राणु द्वारा निषेचित युग्मज से विकसित होने वाले व्यक्ति का कैरियोटाइप तथा आनुवंशिक विकार लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the karyotype and the genetic disorder of an individual who has developed from a zygote formed from an 'XX' egg fertilised by a 'Y' sperm.

key_points: Karyotype: 47, XXY. Genetic disorder: Klinefelter's Syndrome.

sub_questions.solution: When an XX egg (formed due to non-disjunction during meiosis in the female) is fertilised by a Y sperm, the resulting zygote has 47 chromosomes with the sex chromosome complement XXY. The karyotype is 47, XXY, and the individual develops Klinefelter's Syndrome.

sub_questions.text: इस आनुवंशिक विकार के किन्हीं दो अभिलक्षणों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two symptoms of this genetic disorder.

key_points: Male with feminine characteristics (gynaecomastia — development of breast tissue in males) and sterility/infertility due to poorly developed testes.

sub_questions.solution: Two symptoms of Klinefelter's Syndrome are: (1) Gynaecomastia — the affected individual is phenotypically male but develops breast tissue similar to females due to hormonal imbalance; and (2) Infertility — the testes are poorly developed and undescended, leading to azoospermia or very low sperm count, making the individual sterile.

sub_questions.text: इस 'XX' प्रकार के अंडाणु के बनने का संभावित कारण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the possible reason that leads to the formation of this 'XX' egg.

key_points: Non-disjunction of the sex chromosomes (XX) during meiosis I or meiosis II in the mother, resulting in an egg carrying two X chromosomes instead of one.

sub_questions.solution: The XX egg is formed due to non-disjunction of sex chromosomes during meiosis in the mother. During meiosis I, the two X chromosomes fail to separate and move to the same pole, or during meiosis II, the sister chromatids of the X chromosome fail to separate. This results in an egg cell that carries two X chromosomes (XX) instead of the normal single X chromosome.

sub_questions.text: किसी भी विवाद की स्थिति में, ऊतक का एक बहुत छोटा नमूना या रक्त की एक बूँद एक बच्चे के पितृत्व निर्धारित करने में हमारी मदद कर सकती है। कथन को प्रमाणित करने के लिए वैज्ञानिक स्पष्टीकरण प्रदान कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: In case of any dispute, a very small sample of tissue or even a drop of blood can help us to determine the paternity of a child. Provide a scientific explanation to substantiate the statement.

key_points: DNA fingerprinting / DNA profiling can be used. Every individual has a unique DNA sequence. The DNA banding pattern (fingerprint) of the child shares specific bands from both the biological father and mother. By comparing the DNA profiles of the child, the mother, and the alleged father, paternity can be confirmed or denied.

sub_questions.solution: This statement can be scientifically explained through the technique of DNA fingerprinting (DNA profiling). Every individual's genome contains unique repetitive sequences called Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) or microsatellites. These sequences are inherited from both biological parents. When DNA from even a tiny tissue sample or a drop of blood is extracted, amplified using PCR, and subjected to gel electrophoresis after restriction digestion and Southern blotting, it produces a unique pattern of bands called a DNA fingerprint. Since a child inherits half its DNA from its biological father and half from its biological mother, the child's DNA fingerprint will show bands that match both parents. By comparing the banding patterns of the child, the mother, and the alleged father, it is possible to confirm or rule out paternity with very high certainty.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text: (क) डार्विन के प्राकृतिक वरण की संकल्पना के विशिष्ट लक्षणों की सूची बनाइए। (ख) प्राकृतिक वरण द्वारा विकास के अध्ययन में सूक्ष्मजीव समुचित उदाहरण सिद्ध हुए हैं। कारण देते हुए न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) List the salient features of Darwin's theory of natural selection. (b) Microbes have proved to be suitable examples to study evolution by natural selection. Justify giving reasons.

sub_questions.text: डार्विन के प्राकृतिक वरण की संकल्पना के विशिष्ट लक्षणों की सूची बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: List the salient features of Darwin's theory of natural selection.

key_points: Overproduction: organisms produce more offspring than can survive. Natural variation: individuals in a population show variation in traits. Struggle for existence: competition for limited resources. Survival of the fittest: individuals with favourable variations survive and reproduce. Heredity: favourable traits are passed on to offspring, leading to gradual change over generations.

sub_questions.solution: The salient features of Darwin's theory of natural selection are: (1) Overproduction — all organisms have the potential to reproduce in large numbers, far more than can survive. (2) Variation — individuals within a population show natural variation in their traits; some variations are heritable. (3) Struggle for existence — since resources are limited, there is intense competition among individuals for food, space, and mates. (4) Survival of the fittest (Natural Selection) — individuals with favourable variations that help them better adapt to their environment survive and reproduce, while those with unfavourable variations are eliminated. (5) Inheritance — the favourable traits are passed on to offspring, and over successive generations, these traits become more prevalent in the population, leading to evolutionary change.

sub_questions.text: प्राकृतिक वरण द्वारा विकास के अध्ययन में सूक्ष्मजीव समुचित उदाहरण सिद्ध हुए हैं। कारण देते हुए न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Microbes have proved to be suitable examples to study evolution by natural selection. Justify giving reasons.

key_points: Microbes have very short generation times and reproduce rapidly, allowing many generations to be studied in a short period. They develop antibiotic resistance through natural selection — bacteria exposed to antibiotics undergo mutation; resistant individuals survive and multiply, demonstrating evolution in action.

sub_questions.solution: Microbes are ideal models for studying evolution by natural selection because they reproduce at an extremely rapid rate with very short generation times (e.g., E. coli divides every 20 minutes). This allows thousands of generations to be observed within days or weeks in a laboratory. The development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is a classic real-time example of natural selection: when a bacterial population is exposed to an antibiotic, most individuals die, but rare resistant mutants survive and reproduce rapidly, giving rise to an antibiotic-resistant population. This directly demonstrates the principles of variation, selection pressure, and survival of the fittest.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text: (क) तरल प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया (ह्यूमोरल इम्यून रिस्पॉन्स) तथा कोशिका-माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया के बीच विभेद कीजिए। (ख) एक प्रतिरक्षी अणु का व्यवस्थात्मक आरेख बना कर इसके किन्हीं चार भागों को नामांकित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Differentiate between humoral immune response and cell-mediated immune response. (b) Draw a schematic diagram of an antibody molecule and label any four parts.

sub_questions.text: तरल प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया तथा कोशिका-माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया के बीच विभेद कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between humoral immune response and cell-mediated immune response.

key_points: Humoral immune response: mediated by B-lymphocytes; involves production of antibodies (immunoglobulins) that circulate in blood and lymph; effective against extracellular pathogens and toxins.

Cell-mediated immune response: mediated by T-lymphocytes (especially cytotoxic T-cells); does not involve antibodies; effective against intracellular pathogens, transplanted cells, and cancer cells; responsible for graft rejection.

sub_questions.solution: The humoral immune response is mediated by B-lymphocytes (B-cells), which, upon activation by an antigen, differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies (immunoglobulins). These antibodies circulate in the blood and lymph and neutralise extracellular pathogens, toxins, and free viruses. The cell-mediated immune response, on the other hand, is carried out by T-lymphocytes (particularly cytotoxic T-cells or Tc cells) and does not involve the production of antibodies. It is effective against intracellular pathogens (such as viruses hiding inside host cells), cancer cells, and transplanted foreign tissues, and is responsible for the rejection of organ transplants.

sub_questions.text: एक प्रतिरक्षी अणु का व्यवस्थात्मक आरेख बना कर इसके किन्हीं चार भागों को नामांकित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a schematic diagram of an antibody molecule and label any four parts.

key_points: The four parts to label: Heavy chain, Light chain, Variable region (antigen binding site), Constant region, Disulphide bond, Fc region.

sub_questions.solution: An antibody (immunoglobulin) molecule is Y-shaped and consists of four polypeptide chains — two identical heavy chains and two identical light chains — held together by disulphide bonds. The four parts that should be labelled in the schematic diagram are: (1) Heavy chain — the two longer polypeptide chains forming the backbone of the Y; (2) Light chain — the two shorter chains attached to the upper portion of the heavy chains; (3) Variable region (antigen-binding site) — the tips of both arms of the Y, which are unique and bind to specific antigens; and (4) Constant region (Fc region) — the lower stem of the Y, which is responsible for complement activation and interaction with immune cells. A disulphide bond holding the chains together may also be labelled.

questions.solution: See sub-questions above.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित परिच्छेद को पढ़कर नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।

1981 में, संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारियों को कापोसी सारकोमा, त्वचा के कैंसर तथा रुधिर वाहिनियों के कैंसर की दर में वृद्धि का पता चला। इसी प्रकार प्रोटोज़ोआ द्वारा होने वाले एक श्वसनी संक्रमण न्यूमोसिस्टिस न्यूमोनिया के फैलने का भान हुआ। ये दोनों रोग सामान्य जनसंख्या में तो बहुत ही दुर्लभ थे, परन्तु 'प्रतिरक्षा संदमन युक्त' व्यक्तियों में अधिक व्यापक थे। इसके कारण प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र के विकार की पहचान हुई जिसे उपार्जित प्रतिरक्षा न्यूनता संलक्षण (एड्स) का नाम दिया गया।

1983 में, संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका तथा फ्रांस में कार्यरत विषाणुविज्ञों ने 'एड्स' के रोगकारक की पहचान की जिसे अब हम ह्यूमन इम्यूनोडेफिशिएंसी वायरस (एचआईवी) के नाम से जानते हैं। रोग उत्पन्न करने के लिए 'एचआईवी' मानव शरीर पर हमला करने हेतु एक निर्धारित पथ को अपनाते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.

In 1981, the health workers of United States of America had become aware of the increased frequency of Kaposi's sarcoma, cancer of the skin and blood vessels and another disease pneumocystis pneumonia, a respiratory infection caused by a protozoan. Both these diseases were very rare in the general population, but occurred frequently in more severely 'immunosuppressed' individuals. This led to the recognition of the immune system disorder that was named Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

In 1983, virologists working in the USA and France had identified a causative agent for 'AIDS', now known as Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). 'HIV' follows a set path to attack the human body to cause the disease.

sub_questions.text: मानव शरीर में प्रवेश करने के पश्चात् एचआईवी जिस कोशिका समूह पर आक्रमण करता है, उसका नाम लिखिए। इस कोशिका में होने वाली विभिन्न परिघटनाओं को लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the group of cells the HIV attacks after gaining entry into the human body and write the various events that occur within this cell.

key_points: HIV attacks helper T-lymphocytes (T4 or CD4+ cells). Events: HIV uses its RNA as template to produce DNA via reverse transcriptase; the viral DNA integrates into the host cell's genome; the host cell produces new viral RNA and proteins; new viruses bud off, infecting more cells.

sub_questions.solution: After gaining entry into the human body, HIV attacks the helper T-lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells or T4 cells). The following events occur within these cells: the virus attaches to the surface of the helper T-cell and injects its RNA genome into the cell. Using the enzyme reverse transcriptase, the viral RNA is used as a template to synthesise viral DNA (a process called reverse transcription). This viral DNA integrates into the host cell's chromosomal DNA. The integrated viral DNA (provirus) then directs the synthesis of new viral RNA and viral proteins using the host cell's machinery. New virus particles are assembled and bud off from the cell, which then go on to infect other helper T-cells, progressively reducing their number and severely impairing the immune system.

sub_questions.text: एड्स की पहचान करने वाले नैदानिक परीक्षण का विस्तृत रूप लिखिए। रोग के उपचार हेतु वर्तमान में उपलब्ध संभावित उपचार लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the expanded form of the diagnostic test used for detecting AIDS. Write the possible treatment available for the disease at present.

key_points: ELISA stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. Treatment: Anti-retroviral therapy (ART) using drugs such as AZT (Azidothymidine / Zidovudine) can suppress viral replication but cannot cure the disease.

sub_questions.solution: The diagnostic test used for detecting AIDS is ELISA, which stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. This test detects the presence of HIV antibodies in the patient's blood. A positive ELISA result is confirmed by the Western Blot test. Regarding treatment, while there is currently no complete cure for AIDS, anti-retroviral therapy (ART) using drugs such as AZT (Azidothymidine or Zidovudine) is available. ART suppresses viral replication, slows disease progression, and improves the quality and length of life of HIV-positive individuals, but it does not eliminate the virus from the body.

sub_questions.text: इस रोग को फैलने से रोकने के लिए डब्ल्यूएचओ (WHO) द्वारा सुझाए गए किन्हीं दो उपायों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two steps suggested by WHO for preventing the spread of this disease.

key_points: Use of disposable/sterilised needles and syringes to prevent blood-borne transmission. Practising safe sex using condoms and maintaining sexual fidelity to prevent sexual transmission.

sub_questions.solution:
The WHO has suggested several measures to prevent the spread of AIDS. Two important steps are: (1) Use of disposable needles and syringes — sharing of needles and syringes among intravenous drug users is a major route of HIV transmission. Ensuring that only sterile, disposable needles are used prevents blood-borne spread of the virus. (2) Practising safe sex — using condoms consistently during sexual intercourse and limiting the number of sexual partners significantly reduces the risk of sexual transmission of HIV, which is one of the most common routes of spreading the virus.

OR

(c) An AIDS patient does not die of the disease itself but from secondary infections because HIV progressively destroys the helper T-lymphocytes (CD4+ cells), which are central to the body's immune response. As the count of helper T-cells falls drastically over time, the immune system becomes severely compromised and loses the ability to fight even common infections that a healthy immune system would easily control. The patient becomes highly susceptible to opportunistic infections — such as Pneumocystis pneumonia, tuberculosis, fungal infections, and certain cancers — caused by pathogens that a normal immune system would otherwise suppress. It is these secondary opportunistic infections, not the HIV virus itself, that ultimately cause death in AIDS patients.

मानव तथा अन्य सभी कशेरुकियों में शुक्रजनन एक महत्वपूर्ण मूल लैंगिक अभिलक्षण है। इस प्रक्रम का समन्वय तथा नियंत्रण हॉर्मोनों के प्रभाव द्वारा किया जाता है। मनुष्यों में यह किशोरावस्था/यौवनारंभ से प्रारंभ होता है तथा सतत चलता रहता है। भ्रूणीय वृषण में आदि (मौलिक) जनन (जर्म) कोशिकाएँ शुक्राणुजन (स्पर्मैटोगोनिया) में विभेदित हो जाती हैं। शुक्राणुजन (स्पर्मैटोगोनिया) शुक्राणुओं की पूर्ववर्ती हैं। यह शुक्रजनक नलिकाओं की बाह्य स्तर (भित्ति) पर अवस्थित होती हैं जहाँ शुक्रजनन का प्रक्रम संपन्न होता है।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.

Spermatogenesis is an important primary sex characteristic in humans and all other vertebrates. The process is coordinated and controlled under the influence of hormones. It starts with the onset of puberty in humans and thereafter continues. The primordial cells within the embryonic testis which differentiate into spermatogonia are the precursors of the sperms. These are located at the outer walls of the seminiferous tubules where the process of spermatogenesis proceeds.

sub_questions.text: वृषण में एफएसएच के प्रकार्य/क्रिया स्थल तथा बाद में इसके क्रियाकलाप का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the site of action of FSH in the testes and describe its action thereafter.

key_points: FSH acts on the Sertoli cells (nurse cells) lining the seminiferous tubules. It stimulates Sertoli cells to secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP) and other factors that support spermatogenesis and sperm maturation.

sub_questions.solution:
FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) acts on the Sertoli cells, which are the nursing or sustentacular cells lining the seminiferous tubules of the testes. Upon binding to Sertoli cells, FSH stimulates them to secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP), which binds to testosterone and maintains a high local concentration of testosterone within the tubules, essential for spermatogenesis. FSH also promotes the development and maturation of spermatids into functional spermatozoa through the process of spermiogenesis. Thus, FSH plays a crucial role in initiating and maintaining sperm production.

OR

LH (Luteinising Hormone) acts on the Leydig cells (interstitial cells) present in the connective tissue between the seminiferous tubules of the testes. LH stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise and secrete testosterone (the primary male sex hormone). Testosterone is essential for the initiation and maintenance of spermatogenesis, development of male secondary sexual characteristics, and the proper functioning of the male reproductive system.

sub_questions.text: उन कोशिकाओं के नाम तथा उनके उत्पाद लिखिए जो शुक्रजनन के दौरान निम्न प्रक्रम करते हैं : (i) समसूत्री विभाजन तथा विभेदन (ii) अर्धसूत्री विभाजन I तथा अर्धसूत्री विभाजन II
sub_questions.text_english: Name the cells and their products which undergo: (i) Mitosis and Differentiation (ii) Meiosis I and Meiosis II during the process of spermatogenesis.

key_points: (i) Spermatogonia undergo mitosis and differentiation to produce primary spermatocytes. (ii) Primary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis I to produce secondary spermatocytes; secondary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis II to produce spermatids.

sub_questions.solution: (i) Spermatogonia undergo mitosis and differentiation; the product of this process is primary spermatocytes. (ii) Primary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis I to produce secondary spermatocytes; secondary spermatocytes then undergo Meiosis II to produce spermatids (which subsequently differentiate into spermatozoa through spermiogenesis).

sub_questions.text: शुक्रजनक नलिकाओं से मोचित होने के उपरांत शुक्राणुओं को अधिवृषण तक ले जाने वाली सहायक नलिकाओं के नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the accessory ducts that the sperms travel through from seminiferous tubules to reach the epididymis.

key_points: Rete testis and vasa efferentia (efferent ductules) are the accessory ducts through which sperms travel from the seminiferous tubules to reach the epididymis.

sub_questions.solution: After being released from the seminiferous tubules, sperms pass through the rete testis and then through the vasa efferentia (efferent ductules) before reaching the epididymis, where they are stored and undergo maturation.

questions.text: ई. कोलाई तथा जीवाणुभोजी का उपयोग करके 'हर्षे एवं चेस' द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग पर आधारित निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए : (क) (i) उन्होंने अपने प्रयोग में ई. कोलाई के संवर्धन माध्यम में विकिरण सक्रिय सल्फर 35S तथा विकिरण सक्रिय फॉस्फोरस 32P का उपयोग संबंधित माध्यम में क्यों किया, जिन्हें बाद में जीवाणुभोजी द्वारा संक्रमित किया गया ?
questions.text_english: Answer the following questions that are based on 'Hershey and Chase' experiment using E. coli and bacteriophage : (a) (i) Why did they use radioactive sulphur 35S and radioactive phosphorus 32P in their respective culture media for growing E. coli population which subsequently were infected by bacteriophage ?

sub_questions.text: उन्होंने अपने प्रयोग में ई. कोलाई के संवर्धन माध्यम में विकिरण सक्रिय सल्फर 35S तथा विकिरण सक्रिय फॉस्फोरस 32P का उपयोग संबंधित माध्यम में क्यों किया ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did they use radioactive sulphur 35S and radioactive phosphorus 32P in their respective culture media for growing E. coli population which subsequently were infected by bacteriophage ?

key_points: Sulphur is found in proteins (in amino acids cysteine and methionine) but not in DNA. Phosphorus is found in DNA but not in proteins. By using 35S to label proteins and 32P to label DNA separately, they could track which molecule (DNA or protein) entered the bacterial cell during phage infection.

sub_questions.solution: Hershey and Chase used radioactive 35S and 32P because sulphur is a component of proteins (present in amino acids like cysteine and methionine) but is absent from DNA, while phosphorus is a component of DNA (in the phosphate backbone) but is absent from proteins. By growing one batch of E. coli in a medium containing 35S, the bacteriophages grown on them had their protein coats labelled with 35S. Another batch grown in 32P medium had their DNA labelled with 32P. This differential labelling allowed Hershey and Chase to distinguish between the protein coat and the DNA of the phage and determine which material was injected into the bacterium during infection.

sub_questions.text: उनके द्वारा निम्नलिखित के उपयोग करने का उद्देश्य लिखिए : (1) संमिश्रक (2) अपकेंद्रणयंत्र
sub_questions.text_english: State the purpose of their using the following: (1) Blender (2) Centrifuge

key_points: Blender: used to separate the phage coats from the surface of bacteria after infection by shearing off the external phage particles. Centrifuge: used to separate the heavier bacteria (with injected material) from the lighter phage coats by spinning; bacteria pellet at the bottom while phage coats remain in the supernatant.

sub_questions.solution: The blender was used to separate the bacteriophage coats that remained outside the bacterial cells from the bacteria after infection. The shearing force of the blender dislodged the phage ghost (empty protein coats) from the surface of the bacteria. The centrifuge was then used to separate the bacteria (which are heavier) from the phage coats (which are lighter). After centrifugation, the bacteria formed a pellet at the bottom while the phage coats remained in the supernatant, allowing Hershey and Chase to measure radioactivity in each fraction separately.

sub_questions.text: अपने प्रयोग की अवधि में उनके द्वारा किए गए प्रेक्षण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the observations they made during the course of their experiment.

key_points: When bacteria were infected with 35S-labelled phages: the supernatant (phage coats) showed high radioactivity of 35S, while the bacterial pellet showed very little 35S. When infected with 32P-labelled phages: the bacterial pellet showed high radioactivity of 32P, while the supernatant showed little 32P. This showed that DNA was injected into the bacteria while the protein coat remained outside.

sub_questions.solution: During their experiment, Hershey and Chase observed the following: When bacteria were infected with bacteriophages labelled with 35S (protein coat labelled), after blending and centrifugation, the radioactivity of 35S was found predominantly in the supernatant (phage coats), while the bacterial pellet contained very little 35S. This indicated that the protein coat did not enter the bacterium. When bacteria were infected with 32P-labelled phages (DNA labelled), the radioactivity of 32P was found predominantly in the bacterial pellet, while the supernatant had very little 32P. This showed that the viral DNA had been injected into the bacterium, while the protein coat remained outside.

sub_questions.text: अपने प्रयोग के अंत में प्राप्त परिणामों के आधार पर वे जिस निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचे, उसे लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Based on the results, write the conclusion they arrived at the end of their experiment.

key_points: Conclusion: DNA, not protein, is the genetic material that is injected into the host bacterium by the bacteriophage to direct the synthesis of new phage particles. DNA is the hereditary material.

sub_questions.solution: Based on the results of their experiment, Hershey and Chase concluded that DNA, and not protein, is the genetic material. Since the 32P-labelled DNA entered the bacterial cells and directed the production of new bacteriophage particles (including phages with 32P in their DNA), it was clearly the DNA that carried the genetic information. The protein coat (labelled with 35S) remained outside the bacterium and was not transmitted to the progeny phages. This experiment provided conclusive evidence that DNA is the molecule of heredity.

sub_questions.text: असीमकेंद्रकी में प्रारंभन, दीर्घीकरण तथा समापन के संदर्भ में अनुलेखन प्रक्रिया का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the process of transcription in prokaryotes with respect to initiation, elongation and termination.

key_points: Initiation: RNA polymerase with sigma factor recognises and binds to the promoter region on the template strand; DNA unwinds. Elongation: RNA polymerase synthesises RNA in 5' to 3' direction using the template strand (3' to 5'); NTPs are added complementarily. Termination: RNA polymerase reaches the terminator sequence; the newly synthesised RNA is released and the enzyme detaches.

sub_questions.solution: In prokaryotes, transcription occurs in three stages. During initiation, the RNA polymerase holoenzyme (with its sigma factor) recognises and binds to the promoter region (a specific DNA sequence upstream of the gene). The sigma factor facilitates the binding to the correct promoter. Once bound, the DNA double helix unwinds locally, exposing the template strand. During elongation, the RNA polymerase moves along the template strand in the 3' to 5' direction, synthesising a complementary RNA strand in the 5' to 3' direction by adding ribonucleoside triphosphates (NTPs) complementary to the template. The sigma factor is released after initiation, and the core enzyme continues elongation. During termination, the RNA polymerase reaches a specific terminator sequence in the DNA. In rho-independent termination, the newly synthesised RNA forms a hairpin loop structure that causes the polymerase to pause and fall off; in rho-dependent termination, the rho protein facilitates release. The completed RNA transcript is released and RNA polymerase dissociates from the DNA.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित जीवों में अनुलेखन प्रक्रम में कितने प्रकार के आरएनए पॉलीमेरेज़ का उपयोग किया जाता है : (1) असीमकेंद्रकी (2) सुकेंद्रकी
sub_questions.text_english: Write how many types of RNA polymerases are used in transcription in (1) Prokaryotes, (2) Eukaryotes.

key_points: Prokaryotes: 1 type of RNA polymerase (which transcribes all types of RNA). Eukaryotes: 3 types — RNA polymerase I (transcribes rRNA except 5S), RNA polymerase II (transcribes mRNA/hnRNA), RNA polymerase III (transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNA).

sub_questions.solution: In prokaryotes, only one type of RNA polymerase is used for transcription. This single enzyme is responsible for synthesising all types of RNA — mRNA, rRNA, and tRNA. In eukaryotes, three types of RNA polymerases are involved: RNA polymerase I transcribes ribosomal RNA (rRNA), except 5S rRNA; RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor mRNA (pre-mRNA or hnRNA), which is then processed into mature mRNA; and RNA polymerase III transcribes transfer RNA (tRNA), 5S rRNA, and small nuclear RNA (snRNA).

questions.text_english: (a) (i) Why should a cell be made competent to take up an alien DNA ? How can a bacterial cell be made competent using calcium ions ? Explain. (ii) (1) State the importance of gel electrophoresis in biotechnology. (2) Explain the principle on which this technique works. (3) Mention why ethidium bromide is used in this technique.

sub_questions.text: किसी कोशिका को विजातीय (बाहरी) डीएनए लेने हेतु सक्षम क्यों बनाना चाहिए ? कैल्शियम आयन के उपयोग द्वारा किसी जीवाणु कोशिका को कैसे सक्षम बनाया जा सकता है ? व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why should a cell be made competent to take up an alien DNA ? How can a bacterial cell be made competent using calcium ions ? Explain.

key_points: Cells have a cell wall and cell membrane that prevent the entry of foreign DNA. Competence is the ability of a cell to take up DNA. Calcium ions increase the permeability of the bacterial cell membrane, allowing foreign DNA to enter. Bacteria are treated with cold CaCl2 solution and then given a brief heat shock (42°C) to facilitate entry of recombinant DNA.

sub_questions.solution: A cell must be made competent because the bacterial cell wall and cell membrane form a physical barrier that normally prevents the entry of large foreign DNA molecules. Competence refers to the physiological state in which a cell is capable of taking up external DNA. To make a bacterial cell competent using calcium ions, the bacterial cells are first chilled in ice-cold calcium chloride (CaCl2) solution. The calcium ions increase the permeability of the bacterial cell membrane by interacting with the lipopolysaccharides in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. The chilled bacteria are then mixed with the recombinant DNA plasmid and briefly subjected to a heat shock at 42°C for a short duration. This sudden temperature change creates pores in the cell membrane and allows the recombinant DNA to enter the bacterial cell. The cells are then returned to ice to close the pores, trapping the plasmid inside.

sub_questions.text: (1) जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी में जेल वैद्युत कण-संचलन का महत्व लिखिए। (2) उस सिद्धान्त की व्याख्या कीजिए जिस पर यह तकनीक कार्य करती है। (3) इस तकनीक में इथीडियम ब्रोमाइड का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (1) State the importance of gel electrophoresis in biotechnology. (2) Explain the principle on which this technique works. (3) Mention why ethidium bromide is used in this technique.

key_points: Importance: used to separate and analyse DNA, RNA, and protein fragments based on size; essential for confirming the presence of a gene of interest after restriction digestion. Principle: charged molecules (negatively charged DNA) migrate through an agarose/polyacrylamide gel matrix when an electric current is applied; smaller fragments migrate faster and farther. Ethidium bromide: intercalates between DNA bases and fluoresces under UV light, allowing visualisation of DNA bands.

sub_questions.solution: (1) Gel electrophoresis is of great importance in biotechnology as it is used to separate DNA fragments of different sizes produced after restriction enzyme digestion, to confirm the identity and size of PCR-amplified products, and to separate proteins or RNA based on molecular weight. It is an essential tool for DNA fingerprinting, gene cloning, and recombinant DNA technology. (2) The technique works on the principle that DNA molecules are negatively charged due to their phosphate backbone. When placed in an agarose gel matrix and an electric current is applied, DNA fragments migrate from the negative electrode (cathode) toward the positive electrode (anode). Smaller fragments move faster through the gel matrix and travel farther, while larger fragments move slower and remain closer to the origin. This size-based separation creates a pattern of bands. (3) Ethidium bromide is used in this technique as a fluorescent dye that intercalates (inserts itself) between the stacked base pairs of the DNA double helix. When exposed to UV light, the ethidium bromide-DNA complex fluoresces and emits an orange-red colour, making the DNA bands visible under UV light for analysis and documentation.

sub_questions.text: बीटी (Bt) कपास के पौधे को गोलक शलभ कृमि के लिए प्रतिरोधी किस प्रकार बनाया गया ? व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How was Bt cotton plant made resistant to bollworm ? Explain.

key_points: The cry gene (specifically cry1Ac or cry2Ab) from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) was isolated and introduced into the cotton plant genome using recombinant DNA technology. The cry gene encodes a Cry protein (crystal protein/delta endotoxin) that is toxic to bollworm larvae.

sub_questions.solution: Bt cotton was made resistant to bollworm (specifically Helicoverpa species) through genetic engineering using recombinant DNA technology. The cry gene (such as cry1Ac and cry2Ab), which codes for a crystal (Cry) protein also called delta endotoxin, was isolated from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt). This gene was introduced into the cotton plant genome using an appropriate vector (such as the disarmed Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens). The transformed cotton plants (Bt cotton) express the Cry protein in their tissues. When bollworm larvae feed on Bt cotton, they ingest the Cry protein, leading to their death, thereby conferring resistance to the plant.

sub_questions.text: बीटी (Bt) कपास के पौधों को खाने वाले गोलक शलभ कृमियों के मरने की क्रियाविधि का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the mechanism that leads to the death of bollworms feeding on Bt cotton plants.

key_points: The Cry protein produced by the Bt cotton plant is in an inactive protoxin form. When ingested by bollworm larvae, the alkaline pH of the larval midgut activates the protoxin by cleaving it into an active toxin. The active toxin binds to specific receptors on the epithelial cells of the midgut, creating pores that disrupt osmotic balance, causing cell swelling, lysis, and death of the larva.

sub_questions.solution: The Cry protein produced in Bt cotton plants is initially in an inactive form called protoxin. When bollworm larvae feed on the Bt cotton plant and ingest the Cry protein, the alkaline environment of the larval midgut activates the protoxin by proteolytic cleavage, converting it into the active toxic form. The active Cry toxin then binds to specific receptor proteins located on the epithelial cells lining the midgut of the insect. This binding leads to the formation of pores in the cell membrane of the gut epithelial cells. These pores disrupt the osmotic balance of the cells, causing them to swell, lyse (burst), and eventually die. The destruction of the gut lining leads to the death of the bollworm larva, effectively protecting the cotton plant from pest damage.

questions.text: (क) (i) एक आवृतबीजी में वर्तिकाग्र पर परागकण के जनित होने से लेकर द्विनिषेचन तक के प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए तथा अंतिम उत्पादों की सूत्रगुणता (प्लॉइडी) का उल्लेख कीजिए। इस प्रक्रम में सहाय कोशिकाओं की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए। (ii) भ्रूणपोष का विकास भ्रूण के विकास से पहले होता है, क्यों ?

State the role of synergids during the course of the process. (ii) Why does the development of endosperm precede that of the embryo ?

sub_questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी में वर्तिकाग्र पर परागकण के जनित होने से लेकर द्विनिषेचन तक के प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए तथा अंतिम उत्पादों की सूत्रगुणता (प्लॉइडी) का उल्लेख कीजिए। इस प्रक्रम में सहाय कोशिकाओं की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the process of double fertilization in an angiosperm starting from the germination of pollen grains on the stigma, mentioning the ploidy of the end products formed at the end. State the role of synergids during the course of the process.

key_points: Pollen grain lands on stigma and germinates, producing a pollen tube that grows through the style guided by the synergids.
The pollen tube carries two male gametes into the embryo sac through the micropyle.
Synergids secrete chemotropic substances that guide the pollen tube and one synergid degenerates after pollen tube entry.
One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) → diploid zygote (2n).
The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei / secondary nucleus (triple fusion) → triploid primary endosperm nucleus (3n). This process is called double fertilization.

sub_questions.solution: When a pollen grain lands on the stigma of a compatible flower, it germinates. The pollen tube emerges from the germination pore and grows through the style toward the ovary. The pollen tube carries two non-motile male gametes. The synergids (two cells at the micropylar end of the embryo sac) secrete chemotropic substances that guide the pollen tube through the micropyle into the embryo sac. One of the synergids degenerates upon pollen tube entry, allowing the tube to release the two male gametes inside the embryo sac. The first male gamete fuses with the egg cell in a process called syngamy, forming the diploid zygote (2n), which eventually develops into the embryo. The second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (or the secondary nucleus) in a process called triple fusion, forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (3n), which develops into the endosperm. Since two fusions occur simultaneously — syngamy and triple fusion — the entire event is called double fertilization. The role of synergids is to guide the pollen tube chemotropically into the embryo sac and to facilitate the entry and release of the male gametes.

sub_questions.text: भ्रूणपोष का विकास भ्रूण के विकास से पहले होता है, क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does the development of endosperm precede that of the embryo ?

key_points: Endosperm develops before the embryo because it provides the necessary nutrients and nourishment required for the growth and development of the embryo.

sub_questions.solution: Endosperm development precedes that of the embryo because the endosperm serves as the primary nutritive tissue for the developing embryo. The growing embryo requires a continuous supply of nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and other essential compounds) to fuel its cell divisions and differentiation. The endosperm must therefore be established first so that it can provide this nutritional support from the very beginning of embryo development.

sub_questions.text: उस स्थल का उल्लेख कीजिए जहाँ स्त्री (मानव मादा) में अंडाणु का निषेचन होता है। निषेचन प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए और उल्लेख कीजिए कि इस प्रक्रम में अनेक शुक्राणुओं के प्रवेश को कैसे रोका जाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the site where fertilisation of the ovum occurs in a human female. Explain the process of fertilization and mention how polyspermy is prevented.

key_points: Site: Fallopian tube (ampullary region / ampulla). Fertilization: sperm reaches the egg, acrosomal enzymes dissolve the zona pellucida, sperm fuses with egg membrane, secondary oocyte completes meiosis II forming the ovum and second polar body, pronuclei fuse forming zygote. Polyspermy prevention: cortical reaction — cortical granules released after sperm entry change the zona pellucida (zona reaction), making it impermeable to additional sperms.

sub_questions.solution: Fertilisation in a human female occurs in the ampullary region (ampulla) of the fallopian tube. During fertilisation, after intercourse, millions of sperms travel through the vagina, uterus, and into the fallopian tube. When a sperm reaches the secondary oocyte, it releases acrosomal enzymes (hyaluronidase and acrosin) through the acrosome reaction, which dissolve the zona pellucida (the outer covering of the egg). The sperm then fuses with the plasma membrane of the secondary oocyte. This triggers the completion of meiosis II in the secondary oocyte, forming the mature ovum (ootid) and a second polar body. The haploid pronuclei of the sperm and the egg then fuse to form the diploid zygote. Polyspermy (entry of more than one sperm) is prevented by the cortical reaction: immediately after the first sperm fuses with the egg membrane, cortical granules beneath the egg plasma membrane release their contents into the perivitelline space, causing structural changes in the zona pellucida (zona reaction) that make it impermeable to further sperm penetration.

sub_questions.text: भ्रूण की उस अवस्था का नाम लिखिए जिसमें उसका गर्भाशय में अंतरोपण होता है। स्त्री (मानव मादा) में अंतरोपण प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the embryonic stage that gets implanted in the uterus. Explain the process of implantation in a human female.

key_points: Blastocyst is the embryonic stage that gets implanted. Implantation: the blastocyst travels to the uterus and sheds the zona pellucida; its outer trophoblast layer attaches to the endometrium (uterine lining); trophoblast cells proliferate and penetrate the endometrium, embedding the blastocyst; the endometrium undergoes changes to accommodate the embryo.

sub_questions.solution: The embryonic stage that gets implanted in the uterus is the blastocyst. After fertilisation, the zygote undergoes repeated mitotic divisions (cleavage) as it travels through the fallopian tube toward the uterus, forming a morula (solid ball of cells) and then a blastocyst (a hollow sphere with an inner cell mass — the embryoblast — and an outer layer of cells called the trophoblast). The blastocyst reaches the uterus around the 7th day after fertilisation. The zona pellucida degenerates (hatching), exposing the trophoblast. The trophoblast cells adhere to the endometrium (uterine lining, which has been prepared by progesterone and oestrogen) and begin to proliferate and penetrate the uterine wall. The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium, a process called implantation, establishing close contact between the embryo and the mother's uterine lining, eventually forming the placenta for nutrient and gas exchange.
